correctness.rationale: For every N≥2 and gcd(a,N)=1, the parity-adjusted quadratic chirp is periodic. A shifted correlation is a character sum, and all d-periodic phase multipliers remain exact zeros of every nonzero autocorrelation. Fourier differentiating gives the exact real Hessian with eigenvalues 8N sin²(πa^{-1}k²/N); its null Fourier labels are precisely multiples of N/d, since N divides a square exactly on that subgroup. Its kernel is therefore the d-dimensional periodic phase space. The Hessian is positive on its Euclidean orthogonal complement and, by continuity and integration along normal line segments, yields the explicit local quadratic error bound and complete local zero-set classification. The extracted checker confirmed 211 coprime parameter cases through N=26 with numerical errors near machine precision. Numerical checks corroborate but do not establish the infinite theorem; the global CAZAC moduli and optimal stability radius are unproved.

originality.rationale: The original 2010 Gilbert–Rzeszotnik paper supplies Gauss-sequence and biunimodular Fourier context; the original 2015 Führ–Rzeszotnik manuscript develops the squarefree finiteness problem and Gaussian examples; and the directly relevant 2018 Benedetto–Cordwell–Magsino manuscript constructs squareful families. None of the inspected statements proves that all sufficiently nearby Gaussian-phase CAZAC sequences belong exactly to the arithmetic periodic-phase family or derives the exact Fourier Hessian spectrum and transverse stability inequality. In particular, existence of nonconstant families is weaker than local exhaustiveness. No directly dominating archived finding was identified in semantic and alias searches. Residual risk remains for earlier complex-Hadamard defect and cyclic-root formulations.
residual_risks: The original 1995 Björck–Saffari article was not obtained in full; a closely equivalent local statement might exist there or in older cyclic-root literature.
The Gaussian-point nullity could be previously calculated as a defect of circulant complex Hadamard matrices under different equivalence conventions.
No semantic search proves global novelty, and an independent literature audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: The long-studied problem of classifying biunimodular cyclic Fourier vectors includes a canonical class of Gaussian chirps and the difficult global squarefree finiteness question. The theorem determines the complete local Gaussian solution germ for every cyclic length, not merely a newly constructed subfamily; it proves the squarefree-versus-squareful arithmetic dichotomy in infinitesimal flexibility, exact Hessian eigenvalues and normal stability. These results distinguish local rigidity from global finiteness and provide a useful structural local invariant for phase-only Fourier design and cyclic Hadamard geometry.
